topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture, outlines the learning outcomes, and establishes the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how mutations in signaling cascades such as Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinases confer growth signal independence and resistance to growth inhibition.

topics.label: Blocks to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They demonstrate how differentiation blocks in hematopoietic lineages and the intestinal epithelium prevent terminal maturation and sustain proliferation.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: It details how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and the dysregulation of pro- and anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how telomere shortening triggers senescence and how cancer cells bypass this barrier through telomerase reactivation and overcome p53-mediated stress responses.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and complex cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: They introduce complex cancer hallmarks and explore the mechanisms and drivers of metabolic rewiring, including aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the requirement for new blood vessel formation to sustain tumor growth and the regulatory balance between angiogenic activators and inhibitors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They cover the multi-step metastatic cascade, the utility of circulating tumor cells in treatment monitoring, metastatic inefficiency, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of how cancer hallmarks integrate across disease progression and provides closing guidance.
